meta.title: wissfort - An opinionated toast component
meta.description: A minimalist toast component. SVG morphing, spring physics, and a clean API — beautiful by default.

hero.description: A minimalist toast component. SVG morphing, spring physics, and a clean API — beautiful by default.

introduccion.title: Introduction
introduccion.p1: Headless and runtime-dependency-free toast notifications library. The core (wiss) is a pure TypeScript "brain" —state, queue, timers— that knows nothing about the DOM or any framework. The visual layer is interchangeable: by default it brings its own themes (light and dark) or you can choose to inherit the theme from your project via daisyUI or shadcn/ui to adapt to your current design.

sonido_interacciones.title: Sound & Interactions
sonido_interacciones.p1_html: wissfort heavily relies on cuelume for its sound system. This incredible library synthesizes audio live without using heavy .mp3 files, keeping the performance impact completely zero (less than 40 KB uncompressed).
sonido_interacciones.p2: Sound is enabled by default, but if you want to disable it globally, you can do so in the configuration:
sonido_interacciones.p3_html: You can also customize the sound that plays when a single notification is fired by passing the sound name in the sound option:
sonido_interacciones.default_sounds_desc_html: Each toast type comes with a pre-assigned cuelume sound that perfectly fits its intention:
sonido_interacciones.catalogo_desc: Explore all available sounds by clicking on the buttons below. Each will trigger an info toast but with its respective custom sound.

historial.desc: Wissfort keeps a record of the toasts that have appeared on screen. You can access or clear them using the API.

configuracion_global.title: Global Configuration
configuracion_global.desc_html: The toaster() function accepts an object to configure the global behavior of all toasts.
configuracion_global.formato_desc: You can change the aesthetics of the notifications between a wiss design or a "dynamic island" type.
configuracion_global.behavior_desc_html: Controls what happens when the limit is reached. normal stacks the notifications, wiss visually replaces the oldest one with an animation.

temas.title: Themes, daisyUI and shadcn/ui
temas.desc: By default, the library uses its own themes (light and dark) built with Tailwind. This ensures the toasts look good out of the box.
temas.shadcn_desc_html: If you use shadcn/ui (in Tailwind v4 or using absolute/hex/oklch color variables), wiss now includes native support. Set theme: 'shadcn' and the toasts will automatically map their colors to your project variables (like --background, --foreground, --primary, --destructive, etc.):
temas.shadcn_nota_html: Note: If you are using an older version of shadcn where variables only export the raw HSL values (e.g. 0 0% 100%), you can still use theme: 'light' or 'dark' and map the --wiss-* variables in your globals.css file by wrapping them in the hsl() function.
temas.daisyui_desc1_html: If you prefer the toasts to inherit the active daisyUI style (light, dark, cyberpunk, etc.), you can use theme: 'daisy':
temas.daisyui_desc2_html: With theme: 'daisy', wiss injects daisyUI classes (alert, alert-success, alert-error, ...) instead of its own. Thus, the final color is resolved by the daisyUI theme configured in your project.
temas.daisyui_desc3: If you don't need to integrate it with daisyUI or prefer the default wiss styles, simply don't pass the theme property (or use 'light'/'dark') and it will use the default theme.

tailwind.title: Tailwind CSS Configuration
tailwind.desc: The wiss themes come with utility classes built into the library code (node_modules). For styles to apply correctly, you must tell Tailwind to process these files.
tailwind.v4_desc_html: In version 4, Tailwind uses CSS-based configuration. Simply add the @source directive in your main CSS file (where you import tailwind) pointing to the library:
